title: THE MONA · SPEED & SWING
vibe: GREEN · You said bring it, and you gave me the numbers I needed: 8 of 8 rounds on the Olympic chain, grip out before lungs, HR 160 at the 12% peak. So today the run comes FIRST and it's a real runner's session — the Mona Fartlek, descending reps at rising speed, the workout Steve Moneghetti built his career on. Then a four-station ballistic EMOM to hammer the one pattern that's gone stale: the swing. Speed, then power. Get after it.
why: Three things drove today. First, your 07-27 numbers: you finished all 8 rounds of the Olympic chain at 80 lb on your first-ever complex day, which is the top of the target — so that shape is confirmed and it has to advance. But your grip gave out before your lungs did, and that tells me exactly HOW to advance it. Not heavier. You don't have a bell above 40 anyway, and more load just makes the grip fail sooner. The lever is grip ENDURANCE and time under tension, so grip work is now a standing item and it shows up twice today. Second, the coverage ledger: the swing and the pure hinge-ballistic engine haven't been loaded since 07-18 and 07-19, ten days ago, which makes it the most neglected quality you own by a wide margin. Yesterday's cleans were a pull, not a hinge. So the main block is ballistic, rotating, and hinge-first, with a double high pull as the wildcard — a movement that has never once appeared in your log. Third, the run. Yesterday's climb hit HR 160 at 12% grade, which is at or above what your flat two-mile tempo produces, at a fraction of the foot impact — that's the incline finding confirmed with a number. But incline alternates with flat, and today is flat, and you told me you want the run's style to change. So instead of a seventh two-mile tempo you get the Mona Fartlek: 2 x 90 seconds hard, then 3 x 60, then 4 x 30, each block faster than the last, with a genuine float in between instead of a shuffle. It's a real fartlek from a real distance-running tradition, and today's research lens was running and conditioning science, which is where it came from. It runs FIRST, before the bells, because 30-second surges at 9.0 deserve fresh legs and a fatigued speed session at 250 lb is not a trade worth making. Core rotates off yesterday's overhead anti-extension work into the frontal plane — chops, lateral loaded walks, side plank — two of which have never been in this program. One honest gap remains open and I'm not going to pretend otherwise: you still have never run a true steady Zone 2. It doesn't belong on a day you asked me to bring it. It belongs on your next easy day, and I'll put it there.

blocks.title: MOBILITY WARM-UP · HIPS, ANKLES + RUNNING PREP
blocks.meta: ~7 min · Moves Method Day B (ankles/knees/hips) + calf-Achilles care + running drills · the run is first today, so this warm-up actually prepares you to run fast
blocks.text: Today's warm-up has a job it hasn't had before: you're going straight into surges, so this has to get you ready for SPEED, not just loosen you up. Start with the Day B mobility, biased to what yesterday's 12% grade loaded: ankle rolls in a deep squat 10/side · toe squats 30s (calves and toes took a beating on that hill) · calf and Achilles rocks against the wall 10/side · knee drives 10/side · single-leg balance 30s/side · horse-stance squats x10 · shoulder extensions x15. That's about 4 minutes. Then 3 minutes of running prep, which is the part that matters most today: leg swings front-to-back 12/side and side-to-side 12/side · high knees 20 steps · butt kicks 20 steps · A-skips 20 steps · then get on the treadmill and jog 2 minutes easy at 5.5 to 6.0 before the clock starts. Do not walk straight from the floor into a 90-second surge. Your hips and hamstrings need the swings and the skips first.

blocks.title: BLOCK 1 · THE MONA FARTLEK (run first today)
blocks.meta: ~19 min · treadmill · 0% incline · descending reps, RISING speed · float is a RUN, not a shuffle · this is the centerpiece
blocks.format: DESCENDING FARTLEK · 2 × 90s hard / 90s float · 3 × 60s hard / 60s float · 4 × 30s hard / 30s float · speed climbs as the reps shorten
blocks.workRest: The whole point of the Mona is that as the reps get SHORTER, they get FASTER — and the float between them is a real running pace, not a recovery shuffle. Float everything at 6.5. Hard reps: 8.0 for the 90s, 8.5 for the 60s, 9.0 for the 30s. Hit the speed buttons a couple of seconds before each transition so the belt is at pace when the interval starts. Zero incline the whole way — yesterday was the hill, today is flat and fast. Cue a CADENCE of 168 to 172 the entire session, especially on the surges: short quick steps, land under yourself, no reaching. At 250 lb that cue is the cheapest injury insurance you own. Total is about 2.2 miles.

items.name: 0:00–2:00 · Opener
items.detail: 6.0 easy. Roll into it, get the breathing organized, find the cadence. This is inside the 19 minutes.

items.name: 2 × 90s HARD @ 8.0 / 90s float @ 6.5
items.detail: 6 minutes. Roughly 7:10 per mile on your watch when you're at 8.0. This should feel controlled but committed — around your two-mile race effort, not a sprint. The float at 6.5 is about 8:45 per mile: keep RUNNING it. If the float turns into a jog you've made the whole session easier than it's supposed to be.

items.name: 3 × 60s HARD @ 8.5 / 60s float @ 6.5
items.detail: 6 minutes. About 6:45 per mile. Faster than the 90s, shorter to hold. Same float. This is the middle of the session and it's where it starts asking questions.

items.name: 4 × 30s HARD @ 9.0 / 30s float @ 6.5
items.detail: 4 minutes. About 6:20 per mile — faster than anything in your log. Thirty seconds is short; run it like you mean it, then get straight back to 6.5. Four of these back to back with only 30 seconds between is the sting in the tail. Arms driving, tall posture, quick feet.

items.name: 18:00–19:00 · Walk down
items.detail: 3.0 walk for a minute. Don't step off hot.

blocks.text: This is a genuine distance-running workout, not a treadmill interval set invented by a strength coach — it's the session Steve Moneghetti ran on a Tuesday for twenty years, and the reason it works is the descending structure: every block is shorter and faster than the one before, so you're accelerating through the whole thing while getting progressively more tired. The float is what separates it from ordinary intervals. Most people jog the float and turn a continuous 16-minute effort into eight separate hard reps. Run the float at 6.5 and the session becomes one long, undulating, unbroken effort — which is the point, and which is why it builds the top end without needing more miles. You've never run a fartlek in this program. You've run six flat two-mile tempos at essentially one pace, plus one hill. Today changes the axis again: yesterday you got harder by going UP, today you get harder by going FAST for short bites. Your PR pace is 7:29 per mile and your engine has never been the limiter, so the 9.0 reps are a real stretch but they are well inside what you can do. Report back the peak HR and how the 30s felt.

blocks.title: BLOCK 2 · BALLISTIC EMOM (4 stations, rotating)
blocks.meta: ~16 min · 2×40 lb + 16 kg + 50 lb DB · a new station every minute, no rest minutes · GREEN 4 full cycles · YELLOW 3
blocks.format: EMOM · 16 min · one station per minute, rotating 1-2-3-4 · each minute's work should take 30–40s, the rest of the minute is your rest
blocks.workRest: Top of every minute you start the next station. Four stations, four cycles, sixteen straight minutes with no rest minute built in — your rest is whatever's left of each minute after the work, so move with purpose but don't rush the technique. If a minute's work starts bleeding past 45 seconds, drop 2 reps at that station and keep the clock. This format is deliberate: your grip failed first on yesterday's unbroken chain, and 30 seconds on / 30 seconds off is exactly how you train grip endurance without another 18-minute death grip. Same limiter, different exposure.

items.name: MIN 1 · Double Swing ×12
items.detail: 2×40 lb (80 lb) · the most neglected movement in your log — ten days since a real hinge ballistic. Hike both bells back hard, snap the hips, let the arms be ropes. Float to chest height, no higher. Chest tall, glutes hard at the top, do not squat it. Twelve crisp reps, then park them.

items.name: MIN 2 · Double High Pull ×8 (WILDCARD)
items.detail: 2×40 lb · NEW — this has never appeared in your log once. It's a swing that doesn't stop at the top: same hip snap, but as the bells float you pull the elbows high and back so the bells arrive at shoulder height, elbows above the wrists, then guide them back down into the next hike. It's the missing link between a swing and a snatch and it's a genuine upper-back and pull stimulus that a swing never gives you. Eight reps. Keep it a HINGE with a pull on top, not a row.

items.name: MIN 3 · Snatch ×12 (6/side)
items.detail: 16 kg · one hand hikes, hips snap, and the bell travels in one motion to a locked-out overhead punch. Six each side. Light bell, fast reps, full lockout — this is the power station, not a grind. Snatches haven't been in the log since the 07-19 Tabata.

items.name: MIN 4 · Bent-Over Row ×8/side
items.detail: 50 lb DB · hinge over, flat back, brace, and row the DB to the hip — elbow past the ribs, squeeze, control it down. Eight each side. Horizontal pulling is nine days stale and it's the pattern that balances all the pressing you did yesterday. This is also your second grip station of the day: hold the DB hard, no straps, no wrist curl.

blocks.text: Four cycles is sixteen minutes and it is the whole point of the block. The theme is the hinge-ballistic engine — swing, high pull, snatch — which your log has genuinely neglected while you've been doing chains, isolation and unilateral work, plus one horizontal row to balance yesterday's presses and jerks. Every station is grip-forward on purpose. Yesterday told us grip is your limiter on long unbroken work, and the fix isn't avoiding grip, it's training it in a pattern where it gets short repeated breaks and has to come back. Count your cycles. Four is the target and I want the number — that's what tells me whether the next ballistic day adds a fifth cycle or adds reps per station.

blocks.title: CORE · FRONTAL PLANE (chop, carry, side plank)
blocks.meta: ~6 min · 16 kg + 50 lb DB · 3 rounds · two of these three have never been in your program
blocks.format: 3 ROUNDS · move between exercises, rest ~40s between rounds
blocks.workRest: Your last three core blocks were anti-rotation, loaded rotation, then overhead anti-extension. The gap is the FRONTAL plane — resisting sideways bend and moving across your body under load. Both of the first two movements are new to this program, pulled from the muscle-building library. Ribs down, no leaning, let the midline do the work instead of the low back.

items.name: Half-Kneeling Chop
items.detail: 16 kg · 8/side · NEW. Half-kneeling, inside knee down. Hold the bell by the horns and move it diagonally from high outside the up-knee's shoulder down across to the opposite hip, then reverse. Slow and controlled. The hips must NOT rotate — the whole exercise is your midline refusing to let the load twist you. Switch legs each side.

items.name: Suitcase Lateral Walk
items.detail: 50 lb DB · 20 steps out, 20 steps back, each side · NEW. Heavy DB in one hand at your side, and side-step. Do not lean away from the weight and do not hike the shoulder — stand dead vertical and let the opposite obliques fight the tilt. Then switch hands and come back. Grip again, deliberately: this is your third grip exposure and it's a slow one.

items.name: Side Plank Reach-Through
items.detail: bodyweight · 8/side · side plank on the elbow, top arm reaching for the ceiling, then thread it under your torso and rotate, then reach back up. Hips stay HIGH the whole time — the reps are worthless if the hip drops. Eight controlled reaches each side.

blocks.text: Frontal-plane and anti-lateral-flexion midline work, which is the one plane your core hasn't trained recently, and the chop and lateral walk are both new movements pulled straight from the muscle-building library that your kettlebell density days never touch. Three rounds, six minutes, done.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.meta: ~3 min · hamstrings and hips from the surges, forearms from three grip stations
blocks.text: Walk 60s at 3.0, 0%. Then: standing hamstring stretch 30s/side (the 9.0 reps loaded those) · half-kneeling hip flexor 30s/side · calf and Achilles against the wall 30s/side · figure-4 glute stretch 30s/side · forearm and wrist flexor stretch 30s each, both directions — you gripped hard at four stations today and the forearms have earned it · 5 slow nasal breaths on your back. Report back with FOUR things: peak HR on the fartlek and how the four 30-second reps at 9.0 felt, how many full cycles of the ballistic EMOM you finished out of 4, whether the double HIGH PULL felt like a natural movement or a fight, and whether your grip held up better today with the built-in breaks than it did on Monday's unbroken chain. That last one decides how the next chain gets built.

timer.emomUnit: Block 2 is a real EMOM — set it to 16 minutes and rotate stations every minute (swing → high pull → snatch → row). Block 1 is the fartlek: use the countdown or just watch the treadmill clock and change speed at each transition. Block 3 is 3 rounds by feel.
